sourceEvidence.title: 2AR-FE Water-Pump Active-Leak and Bearing Diagnosis
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Inspect the rest of the cooling system before condemning the pump. Check reservoir level, pulley/bearing play and smoothness, and press a dry paper towel against cleaned pump-area residue. Dry residue alone does not require replacement; wet coolant, an active drip, excessive bearing play, or rough rotation does. If replacement is confirmed, use the model-year repair procedure and verify the pump and separately sold gasket by VIN. Toyota lists exact pump assembly 16100-09515, but the part page itself requires a vehicle-fitment check. Do not automatically replace the belt, tensioner, thermostat, or coolant as separate failures without inspecting them.

sourceEvidence.title: 2GR-FE Water-Pump Active-Leak and Bearing Diagnosis
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Inspect the full cooling system before condemning the pump. Check coolant level and other leak sources, test the pump bearing for free play and smooth rotation, clean the residue, and use a dry paper towel to determine whether coolant is still wet. Dry residue alone does not require replacement. If an active leak or bearing failure is confirmed, follow the model-year repair procedure and verify the pump and separately sold gasket by VIN. Toyota lists current pump 16100-09442 and previous version 16100-09441. Do not automatically add a thermostat, thermostat gasket, or coolant retail claim unless the actual service inspection and procedure require it.
